setlist.title: He Was A Friend Of Mine

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **He Was A Friend Of Mine** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Nice rendition, but the recording cuts off near the very end; Drum stick pops are audible during the song [1][4][14]
- **Golden Road To Unlimited Devotion** (3 reviews): Energetic little tune that the band oddly didn't keep in its repertoire longer; Hearing it live is a treat, with spirited vocals by Jerry, leading into New Potato [10][12][14]
- **New Potato Caboose** (1 review): Already a fully realized showpiece at this point [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Golden Road To Unlimited Devotion**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd67-05-05.sbs.yerys.1595.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 4 songs; 31 min; rated 4.3/5 by 42 [1]. Said about its sound: Bass is somewhat oversaturated, yet every player is clearly audible; Phil sounds especially energetic at Alligator's opening; Sound quality is not the best; Sound is marginal, but the best available for this transitional period [4][6][7][15]
- **gd1967-05-05.126250.sbd.wolfe-smith.flac16**: soundboard; 4 songs; 32 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1967-05-05.126263.sbd.wolfe-smith.flac24**: soundboard; 4 songs; 32 min; rated 2.6/5 by 5 [3]

## Around the show

- The stage banter is amusing [4]
- Reviewer had the stage banter on a circa-1981 college bootleg; it includes the crowd being told to say a profanity [8]
- Pig Pen's organ playing is clearly audible and sounds like a Hammond, before TC joined the band [10]
- Stage patter is a twisted stand-up routine, showing the band and audience in the same state [15]
- Blair Jackson's book cites Deadbase dating Alligator's first appearance to early June at the Au Go-Go in New York; this May tape contradicts that [5]
- Deadbase lists only three live Golden Road performances, on 3/18, 4/12 and 6/15 in 1967, with no 5/5/67 entry [6]
- Deadbase lists 6/15/67 for this material, saying the actual date and location are unknown [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd67-05-05.sbs.yerys.1595.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Ben Yerys; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Teddy GoodBear speculated the song order from a late-70s tape and its cuts [1]
- **gd1967-05-05.126250.sbd.wolfe-smith.flac16**: taped by Don Wolfe; transferred by Matt Smith; source: Don Wolfe's 3.75 ips > Akai GX636 direct tape head output > Bottlehead tube tape pre pair Tesla tubes circa 1980 > Apogee Mini Me 24/96 > Apogee Mini DAC… [2]. Also: Don Wolfe first circulated it, from a classmate in his early-70s U of O Grateful Dead class; original source unknown [2]
- **gd1967-05-05.126263.sbd.wolfe-smith.flac24**: taped by Don Wolfe; transferred by Matt Smith; source: Don Wolfe's 3.75 ips > Akai GX636 direct tape head output > Bottlehead tube tape pre pair Tesla tubes circa 1980 > Apogee Mini Me 24/96 > Apogee Mini DAC… [3]
